brief: Goldman's Codacci-Pisanelli argues equities can squeeze higher into year-end despite a challenging macro backdrop, because US prime-book positioning has undergone one of the most aggressive deleveraging episodes in a decade, leaving it considerably cleaner. That cleaner positioning combines with three other tailwinds: historically supportive year-end seasonality, returning corporate buybacks (S&P 500 demand estimated near $5bn per day, with 90% of companies expected back in their repurchase window by Monday), and a market that has absorbed hotter CPI, hawkish Fed commentary, surging yields, an oil rally and negative Nvidia headlines without sustained selling. The semiconductor trade has also reset hard in both positioning and valuations, which Goldman says creates room for a squeeze even without the AI monetization and ROI debate resolving before the next earnings cycle. The note's core thesis is that the next rally would be driven by positioning and flows, not fundamentals. Nomura adds a caveat: hedging flows from exotic and structured products can force dealers to buy volatility as equities rally and sell it as markets decline, so a positive spot-vol correlation means even the upside could turn disorderly.
